items.rationale: The model holds no state between calls, and a new session starts with an empty history, so only what the program saved and reloaded would carry over. Options a, b and d each credit the model or the window with a memory it does not have.
The inputs are 1,000; 1,500; 2,000; 2,500; 3,000, which sum to 10,000. By formula, 5 x 1,000 + 500 x (5 x 4 / 2) = 5,000 + 5,000. An answer of 3,000 is only the last call.

Permission to use risky equipment rests on the authoritative training record, read through a tool at the time of the decision. A saved note is a copy that can be stale, and a claim or a confirmation from the student is not the record. The note may only remind the assistant which record to check.

items.answer: Every call is billed for all tokens in the context, so a whole manual costs far more; and long contexts make recall of the relevant passage worse.
accepted: cheaper and the model recalls better

items.rationale: Two valid reasons: cost grows with the tokens sent on every call, and recall degrades as context grows (context rot, relevant text buried in the middle). A manual that exceeds the window is a third valid reason.
Recall is the share of the relevant chunks that were retrieved: 2 of 4 = 0.5. An answer of 0.4 is the precision, 2 of 5.
